core: Both communities run controlled single-fault injection tests: at a fixed point mid-task they insert one specific anomalous event (an operational error or a corrupted/conflicting data item) into an otherwise normal agent trajectory, then evaluate how the agent handles that particular injected anomaly relative to the rest of its work.
quote_core_1: we've been running ⟦T1⟧ on the same deploy pipeline, injecting a 503 from the artifact registry at minute six and a timeout on the health check at minute eleven
quote_core_2: each trajectory received one malformed citation record after the fourth repository query. The ⟦T2⟧ was passed by 39 agents, whose final tables excluded the malformed record or explicitly marked it unresolved.
residue_1: Community 1's usage centers on operational/infrastructure failures (503s, timeouts) and scores agents by how fast they resume normal task progress afterward, i.e. time-to-recovery.
quote_residue_1: we're not measuring whether it fails, we're measuring time-to-recovery, and right now we're at a median of 94 seconds versus 340 seconds three months ago.
residue_2: Community 2's usage centers on corrupted or contradictory data content and scores agents by a binary pass/fail on whether that specific bad item was excluded, quarantined, or flagged in the final output.
quote_residue_2: The ⟦T2⟧ pass rate was 0.81, based solely on whether the final ledger quarantined or flagged that row.
